# ️ Clean Architecture Rules — Tawasol Backend (.NET Core Web API) **Version:** 1.0 **Stack:** .NET Core Web API · Entity Framework Core · Clean Architecture **Author:** Mahmoud Saeed Yousef
---
## ⚠️ CRITICAL: AI Agent Instructions
You are assisting in developing the **Tawasol** backend — a social solidarity platform for rural Egyptian communities.
**Your primary duty is to enforce Clean Architecture at all times.** - If a request violates any rule below → **refuse, explain why, and suggest the correct approach.** - If you are unsure which layer a piece of code belongs to → **ask before writing.** - Never sacrifice architecture for convenience or speed.
---
## Layer Structure
The solution is organized into **4 projects (layers)**. Each layer has strict boundaries.
``` Tawasol.sln ├── Tawasol.Domain # Layer 1 — The Core (innermost) ├── Tawasol.Application # Layer 2 — Business Logic ├── Tawasol.Infrastructure # Layer 3 — External Concerns └── Tawasol.API # Layer 4 — Entry Point (outermost) ```
### Dependency Rule (THE most important rule) Dependencies flow **inward only**: ``` API → Application → Domain Infrastructure → Application → Domain ``` - `Domain` depends on **nothing**. - `Application` depends only on `Domain`. - `Infrastructure` depends on `Application` and `Domain`. - `API` depends on `Application` and `Infrastructure` (only for DI registration).
**NEVER allow an inner layer to reference an outer layer.**
---
## ️ Layer 1: Domain
**Purpose:** The heart of the system. Contains pure business logic with zero external dependencies.
**Allowed in this layer:** - Entities - Value Objects - Enums - Domain Exceptions - Repository Interfaces - Domain Events (if needed)
**Folder Structure:** ``` Tawasol.Domain/ ├── Entities/ │ ├── User.cs │ ├── Case.cs │ ├── Transaction.cs │ └── Notification.cs ├── Enums/ │ ├── UserRole.cs │ ├── CaseStatus.cs │ └── TransactionStatus.cs ├── Interfaces/ │ ├── Repositories/ │ │ ├── IUserRepository.cs │ │ ├── ICaseRepository.cs │ │ └── ITransactionRepository.cs │ └── IUnitOfWork.cs └── Exceptions/ ├── DomainException.cs └── NotFoundException.cs ```
### ✅ Domain Rules
**DO:** - Keep entities as rich domain objects with validation logic inside them. - Define repository interfaces here (`IUserRepository`, `ICaseRepository`, etc.) - Use private setters on entity properties to protect invariants. - Throw `DomainException` for business rule violations.
**NEVER:** - Add `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` in this layer. - Reference any NuGet packages (except possibly FluentValidation for Value Objects). - Add DTOs, ViewModels, or request/response models here. - Write database queries inside entities. - Make entities inherit from any EF Core base class.
**Example — Correct Entity:** ```csharp // ✅ CORRECT public class Case { public Guid Id { get; private set; } public string Title { get; private set; } public decimal TargetAmount { get; private set; } public decimal CollectedAmount { get; private set; } public CaseStatus Status { get; private set; }
private Case() { } // EF Core needs this
public Case(string title, decimal targetAmount) { if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(title)) throw new DomainException("Case title cannot be empty."); if (targetAmount <= 0) throw new DomainException("Target amount must be positive.");
Id = Guid.NewGuid(); Title = title; TargetAmount = targetAmount; Status = CaseStatus.Pending; CollectedAmount = 0; }
public void ApproveByHakim() { if (Status != CaseStatus.Pending) throw new DomainException("Only pending cases can be approved."); Status = CaseStatus.Published; } } ```
```csharp // ❌ WRONG — Database logic inside entity public class Case { public async Task<List<Case>> GetAllCases(AppDbContext context) // NEVER { return await context.Cases.ToListAsync(); } } ```
---
## ️ Layer 2: Application
**Purpose:** Orchestrates use cases. Tells the system *what* to do, not *how* to do it.
**Allowed in this layer:** - Use Cases / Commands / Queries (CQRS pattern using MediatR) - DTOs (Request and Response models) - Application Service Interfaces - Mapping Profiles (AutoMapper) - Validators (FluentValidation) - Custom Application Exceptions
**Folder Structure:** ``` Tawasol.Application/ ├── Features/ │ ├── Cases/ │ │ ├── Commands/ │ │ │ ├── CreateCase/ │ │ │ │ ├── CreateCaseCommand.cs │ │ │ │ ├── CreateCaseCommandHandler.cs │ │ │ │ └── CreateCaseCommandValidator.cs │ │ │ └── ApproveCase/ │ │ │ ├── ApproveCaseCommand.cs │ │ │ └── ApproveCaseCommandHandler.cs │ │ └── Queries/ │ │ └── GetCaseById/ │ │ ├── GetCaseByIdQuery.cs │ │ └── GetCaseByIdQueryHandler.cs │ ├── Donations/ │ └── Auth/ ├── DTOs/ │ ├── Cases/ │ │ ├── CaseResponseDto.cs │ │ └── CreateCaseRequestDto.cs │ └── Common/ │ └── PaginatedResponseDto.cs ├── Interfaces/ │ └── Services/ │ ├── INotificationService.cs │ ├── IFileStorageService.cs │ └── IAuthService.cs ├── Mappings/ │ └── CaseMappingProfile.cs ├── Validators/ │ └── CreateCaseCommandValidator.cs └── Common/ └── Exceptions/ ├── ValidationException.cs └── ForbiddenException.cs ```
### ✅ Application Rules
**DO:** - Use **CQRS** with MediatR: every action is either a `Command` (write) or a `Query` (read). - One folder per feature, one class per use case. - Handlers call repository interfaces (from Domain), never DbContext directly. - Define interfaces for external services (`INotificationService`, `IFileStorageService`) — implement them in Infrastructure. - Use FluentValidation for all input validation.
**NEVER:** - Import or reference `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` in this layer. - Use `AppDbContext` directly inside any handler or service. - Return entity objects from handlers — always map to DTOs. - Put HTTP-specific logic (`HttpContext`, `IActionResult`) here. - Write SQL queries or LINQ-to-SQL in this layer.
**Example — Correct Command Handler:** ```csharp // ✅ CORRECT public class CreateCaseCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateCaseCommand, CaseResponseDto> { private readonly ICaseRepository _caseRepository; private readonly IUnitOfWork _unitOfWork; private readonly IMapper _mapper;
public CreateCaseCommandHandler( ICaseRepository caseRepository, IUnitOfWork unitOfWork, IMapper mapper) { _caseRepository = caseRepository; _unitOfWork = unitOfWork; _mapper = mapper; }
public async Task<CaseResponseDto> Handle(CreateCaseCommand request, CancellationToken ct) { var newCase = new Case(request.Title, request.TargetAmount); await _caseRepository.AddAsync(newCase, ct); await _unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync(ct); return _mapper.Map<CaseResponseDto>(newCase); } } ```
```csharp // ❌ WRONG — DbContext directly in handler public class CreateCaseCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateCaseCommand, CaseResponseDto> { private readonly AppDbContext _context; // NEVER inject DbContext here
public async Task<CaseResponseDto> Handle(CreateCaseCommand request, CancellationToken ct) { var newCase = new Case(request.Title, request.TargetAmount); _context.Cases.Add(newCase); // NEVER write EF logic in Application await _context.SaveChangesAsync(ct); ... } } ```
---
## ️ Layer 3: Infrastructure
**Purpose:** Implements all external concerns — database, storage, notifications, external APIs.
**Allowed in this layer:** - EF Core DbContext and Configurations - Repository Implementations - Unit of Work Implementation - Migrations - External Service Implementations (Firebase push notifications, file storage, etc.)
**Folder Structure:** ``` Tawasol.Infrastructure/ ├── Persistence/ │ ├── AppDbContext.cs │ ├── Configurations/ # IEntityTypeConfiguration per entity │ │ ├── CaseConfiguration.cs │ │ ├── UserConfiguration.cs │ │ └── TransactionConfiguration.cs │ ├── Repositories/ │ │ ├── BaseRepository.cs │ │ ├── CaseRepository.cs │ │ └── UserRepository.cs │ ├── UnitOfWork.cs │ └── Migrations/ ├── Services/ │ ├── NotificationService.cs # Implements INotificationService │ ├── FileStorageService.cs # Implements IFileStorageService │ └── AuthService.cs └── DependencyInjection.cs # Extension method to register all Infrastructure services ```
### ✅ Infrastructure Rules
**DO:** - Implement every interface defined in `Domain` and `Application`. - Use `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` in separate configuration files — **never configure entities inside `OnModelCreating` directly.** - Use a generic `BaseRepository<T>` to avoid repeating CRUD logic. - Keep `AppDbContext` internal to this layer — it must never leak to Application or API. - Register all services via `AddInfrastructure(IServiceCollection services)` extension method.
**NEVER:** - Expose `AppDbContext` to Application or API layers. - Put business logic inside repositories (no if-statements about business rules). - Use Data Annotations on entities (`[Required]`, `[MaxLength]`) — use Fluent API in configurations instead. - Bypass the repository pattern and call DbContext from outside Infrastructure.
**Example — Correct Repository:** ```csharp // ✅ CORRECT public class CaseRepository : BaseRepository<Case>, ICaseRepository { public CaseRepository(AppDbContext context) : base(context) { }
public async Task<IEnumerable<Case>> GetPublishedCasesAsync(CancellationToken ct) { return await _context.Cases .Where(c => c.Status == CaseStatus.Published) .AsNoTracking() .ToListAsync(ct); } } ```
```csharp // ❌ WRONG — Business logic inside repository public async Task ApproveCaseAsync(Guid caseId) { var c = await _context.Cases.FindAsync(caseId); c.Status = CaseStatus.Published; // Business logic belongs in Domain entity if (c.CollectedAmount >= c.TargetAmount) // Business rule — belongs in Domain SendNotification(); // Infrastructure concern mixed with business logic await _context.SaveChangesAsync(); } ```
**Example — Correct Entity Configuration:** ```csharp // ✅ CORRECT — Separate configuration class public class CaseConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<Case> { public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<Case> builder) { builder.HasKey(c => c.Id); builder.Property(c => c.Title).IsRequired().HasMaxLength(200); builder.Property(c => c.TargetAmount).HasColumnType("decimal(18,2)"); builder.Property(c => c.Status).HasConversion<string>(); } } ```
```csharp // ❌ WRONG — Configuring everything in OnModelCreating protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder) { modelBuilder.Entity<Case>().HasKey(c => c.Id); // Pollutes DbContext modelBuilder.Entity<Case>().Property(c => c.Title)...; // Not scalable } ```
---
## ️ Layer 4: API (Presentation)
**Purpose:** Entry point. Handles HTTP requests and routes them to Application layer.
**Allowed in this layer:** - Controllers - Middleware (Exception handling, Logging) - Filters - Program.cs / DI registration - API-specific models if needed (rare — prefer Application DTOs)
**Folder Structure:** ``` Tawasol.API/ ├── Controllers/ │ ├── CasesController.cs │ ├── DonationsController.cs │ └── AuthController.cs ├── Middleware/ │ └── GlobalExceptionMiddleware.cs ├── Filters/ │ └── ValidationFilter.cs └── Program.cs ```
### ✅ API Rules
**DO:** - Controllers are **thin** — they only receive requests, send to MediatR, and return responses. - Use `[ApiController]` and route attributes on all controllers. - Use `IMediator` to dispatch commands and queries — never inject repositories or DbContext here. - Handle all exceptions globally via `GlobalExceptionMiddleware`. - Return standardized response wrappers (e.g., `ApiResponse<T>`).
**NEVER:** - Inject `AppDbContext`, Repositories, or any Infrastructure service directly into Controllers. - Write business logic or validation logic inside Controllers. - Catch exceptions individually in each controller — use global middleware. - Return raw entity objects from endpoints — always use DTOs.
**Example — Correct Controller:** ```csharp // ✅ CORRECT [ApiController] [Route("api/[controller]")] public class CasesController : ControllerBase { private readonly IMediator _mediator;
public CasesController(IMediator mediator) { _mediator = mediator; }
[HttpPost] public async Task<IActionResult> Create([FromBody] CreateCaseCommand command) { var result = await _mediator.Send(command); return CreatedAtAction(nameof(GetById), new { id = result.Id }, result); }
[HttpGet("{id:guid}")] public async Task<IActionResult> GetById(Guid id) { var result = await _mediator.Send(new GetCaseByIdQuery(id)); return Ok(result); } } ```
```csharp // ❌ WRONG — Fat controller with direct DB access [HttpPost] public async Task<IActionResult> Create([FromBody] CreateCaseRequestDto dto) { var newCase = new Case { Title = dto.Title }; // Business logic in controller _context.Cases.Add(newCase); // DbContext in controller — NEVER await _context.SaveChangesAsync(); return Ok(newCase); // Returning entity — NEVER } ```
---
## Naming Conventions
| Artifact | Convention | Example | |---|---|---| | Command | `{Action}{Entity}Command` | `CreateCaseCommand` | | Query | `Get{Entity}By{Criteria}Query` | `GetCaseByIdQuery` | | Handler | `{Command/Query}Handler` | `CreateCaseCommandHandler` | | Repository Interface | `I{Entity}Repository` | `ICaseRepository` | | Repository Implementation | `{Entity}Repository` | `CaseRepository` | | Service Interface | `I{Name}Service` | `INotificationService` | | Service Implementation | `{Name}Service` | `NotificationService` | | Response DTO | `{Entity}ResponseDto` | `CaseResponseDto` | | Request DTO | `{Action}{Entity}RequestDto` | `CreateCaseRequestDto` | | EF Configuration | `{Entity}Configuration` | `CaseConfiguration` | | Validator | `{Command}Validator` | `CreateCaseCommandValidator` |
---
## Global NEVER-DO List
These rules apply across ALL layers. If asked to violate any of them, refuse and explain:
1. **NEVER** inject `AppDbContext` outside of Infrastructure. 2. **NEVER** write business rules inside Controllers, Repositories, or Handlers. 3. **NEVER** skip the repository — always go through `IXxxRepository`. 4. **NEVER** return domain Entities from API endpoints — always map to DTOs. 5. **NEVER** put multiple use cases in one Handler class. 6. **NEVER** reference an outer layer from an inner layer. 7. **NEVER** use `dynamic` or anonymous types for data passing between layers. 8. **NEVER** use `var` when the type is not obvious from the right-hand side. 9. **NEVER** use Data Annotations on Domain entities — use Fluent API. 10. **NEVER** put more than one responsibility in a single class (Single Responsibility Principle). 11. **NEVER** write raw SQL strings unless absolutely necessary and documented. 12. **NEVER** use `static` classes or methods for business logic. 13. **NEVER** commit or generate migration files without confirming the entity configurations are complete.
---
## ✅ Pre-Code Checklist
Before writing any code, answer these questions:
1. Which layer does this code belong to? 2. Does it depend only on inner layers? 3. Is there an interface for this if it crosses layer boundaries? 4. Is there a handler/use case already for this — or should I create a new one? 5. Will the response be mapped to a DTO before leaving the Application layer?
---
## Approved NuGet Packages
| Package | Layer | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `MediatR` | Application | CQRS Commands & Queries | | `AutoMapper` | Application | Entity ↔ DTO mapping | | `FluentValidation` | Application | Input validation | | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` | Infrastructure ONLY | ORM | | `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer` | Infrastructure ONLY | SQL Server provider | | `Swashbuckle.AspNetCore` | API | Swagger UI |
**Do NOT add any package to a layer without checking it fits that layer's responsibility.**
---
## Correct Request Flow
Every request must follow this exact flow:
``` HTTP Request ↓ [API] Controller ↓ (sends Command/Query via IMediator) [Application] Handler ↓ (calls via Interface) [Domain] Entity / Repository Interface ↑ (implemented by) [Infrastructure] Repository / DbContext ↓ Database ↑ [Infrastructure] Returns Entity ↑ [Application] Maps to DTO ↑ [API] Returns HTTP Response ```
**If your code skips any step in this flow → stop and restructure.**
---
*This file is the single source of truth for the Tawasol backend architecture.* *All AI agents must treat these rules as non-negotiable constraints.*
